title: Islanded operation
description: An island separated from the Nordic synchronous area: Nordic FCR, LFDD and protection settings with reserves dimensioned from the island's own demand and largest unit, island aFRR able to replace the largest unit, and Nordic FFR from storage.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485 (SO GL), Annex III
sources.note: A 0.1 s sub-step and a 120 s catch-up limit are Leitbild modelling choices; they resolve the 0.24 Hz/s RoCoF of the reference incident and the FCR-D activation lag. SO GL Annex III (Nordic: time to restore frequency 15 min, standard range ±100 mHz) frames the time scales.

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Table 7 of the FCR requirements models load frequency dependence Kf = 0.01 p.u./Hz (1 %/Hz) with Sn 42,000 MW / 190,000 MWs and 23,000 MW / 120,000 MWs.

sources.title: Nordic TSOs: Requirements for minimum inertia in the Nordic power system (August 2025)
sources.note: Nordic kinetic energy 2020-24: minimum 110-138 GWs, average 190-195 GWs; design levels 150 GWs (FCR-D performance) and 120 GWs (stability).

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Table 1: FCR-N linear from 0 % at 50.0 Hz to 100 % at 49.9/50.1 Hz; no deadband is allowed and the response must not be artificially delayed.

sources.title: Fingrid: Frequency Containment Reserves (FCR) products
sources.note: Indicative FCR-N response about 63 % within 1 minute and 95 % within 3 minutes, i.e. a 60 s first-order lag. The new requirements specify FCR-N dynamics in the frequency domain instead (disturbance profile 1/(70s+1)).

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: Table 1: FCR-D up 49.9 to 49.5 Hz, down 50.1 to 50.5 Hz. Requirement 2: at least 0.86 of steady-state response 7.5 s after the start of a 0.24 Hz/s ramp from 49.9 Hz to 49.0 Hz; the slowest compliant first-order lag is 3.37 s, so 3.3 s is used (derived).

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/631 (NC RfG), Article 13
sources.note: Article 13(1)(a) Table 2, Nordic: 47.5-48.5 Hz 30 min; 48.5-49.0 Hz TSO-specified, at least 30 min; 49.0-51.0 Hz unlimited; 51.0-51.5 Hz 30 min. Generators may disconnect outside these ranges.

sources.title: Statnett: Nasjonal veileder for funksjonskrav i kraftsystemet (NVF 2025)
sources.note: NVF 2025 Table 12-4 (Norway): 47.5-49.0 Hz 30 min; 51.0-52.5 Hz 30 min; synchronous units withstand ±1.5 Hz/s over 1 s.

sources.title: Fingrid: Grid Code Specifications for Power Generating Facilities VJV2024 (unofficial translation 15.1.2025)
sources.note: VJV2024 §10.2.3: withstand 2.0 Hz/s; RoCoF protection may trip only above 4 Hz/s lasting at least 250 ms.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/631 (NC RfG), Article 13
sources.note: The 0.5 s delay of the 47.5 Hz and 51.5 Hz instantaneous elements is a modelling choice; the codes set withstand ranges, not relay delays.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/2196 (NC ER), Annex and Article 15
sources.note: Annex, Nordic: start 48.7-48.8 Hz with 5 % of load, final 48.0 Hz with 30 % cumulative, at least 2 steps, at most 15 % per step. Article 15(7)(a): no intentional time delay beyond relay and breaker operating time.

sources.title: Nordic SOA Annex Emergency and Restoration, revised 11/12/2024
sources.note: Nordic LFDD design: five steps at 48.8 / 48.6 / 48.4 / 48.2 / 48.0 Hz, the first four aiming at 5 % each. The 10 % at 48.0 Hz is derived so that the cumulative disconnection reaches the NC ER 30 %.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2016/1388 (Demand Connection Code), Article 19
sources.note: Article 19(1)(c): LFDD relays operate within 150 ms; used as the stage delay.

sources.title: Technical Requirements for Frequency Containment Reserve Provision in the Nordic Synchronous Area, v1.1 (28 March 2025)
sources.note: FCR-N is 1.43 % of island demand: the 600 MW Nordic requirement over the 42,000 MW system size of Table 7, so FCR-N strength scales with the island.

sources.title: Svenska kraftnät: How is the FCR volume requirement determined?
sources.note: FCR-D must cover the reference incident; for an island this is taken as the output of its largest synchronised unit in each direction.

sources.title: Statnett: Technical product and interface specification for delivery of aFRR to Statnett, v4.0 (June 2023)
sources.note: Table 1: aFRR full activation 300 s maximum (120 s preferred); set-points sent no more often than every 4 s, used as the controller cycle.

sources.title: Nordic FRR dimensioning methodology under SO GL Article 157 (2022)
sources.note: Without neighbours the island restores frequency itself: aFRR equals its largest unit output so that it can replace that unit within the 300 s full activation time.

sources.title: Fingrid: Terms and conditions for providers of manual frequency restoration reserve (30.9.2026)
sources.note: §7.3.1: mFRR full activation time 12.5 min (2.5 min preparation and 10 min ramp), used as preparationSeconds 150 and fullActivationSeconds 750; minimum bid 1 MW.

sources.title: Nordic FRR dimensioning methodology under SO GL Article 157 (2022)
sources.note: mFRR equals the largest unit output so that it can take over FCR and aFRR after the island's dimensioning incident.

sources.title: Nordic SOA Annex Load-Frequency Control & Reserves (LFCR) v8
sources.note: §13.4.1: FFR trigger 49.7 Hz with full activation within 1.30 s (49.6 Hz / 1.00 s and 49.5 Hz / 0.70 s also allowed); short-duration support at least 5 s with deactivation at most 20 %/s; ready again within 15 min.

sources.title: TestGuy: Sync Check Relay (25) Fundamentals and Testing Explained
sources.note: Sync check relays require a slip of 0.1 Hz or less between the sources to operate; used as the frequency-difference limit for closing between two energised islands.

sources.title: Industrial Monitor Direct: Generator breaker closing, power angle and voltage limits
sources.note: No universal angle: some systems accept no more than 20°; manual reclosing in normal operation with digital relays uses 15-25°, automatic synch-check relays 15-35°; a digital-relay example uses 15° and 0.05 Hz. 20° for closing a loop inside one island is a modelling choice within these ranges.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485 (SO GL), Article 25
sources.note: Article 25(1)(c): operational security limits include current limits in terms of thermal rating including the transitory admissible overloads. The emergency rating and its duration (Model, or 900 s for v1 Models as in the v2 build's 120 %/15 min rule) are that transitory admissible overload; the definite-time element trips a branch above it for longer than its duration.

sources.title: CIGRE Technical Brochure 601: Guide for thermal rating calculations of overhead lines
sources.note: TB 601 treats transient conductor heating; the brochure is paywalled and was not read. Overhead conductor time constants are commonly quoted at 5-15 min, so 600 s is used for lines; 7200 s for cables, transformers and v1 HVDC branches stands for their much larger thermal mass. The thermal trip level is derived per branch so that a branch carrying its continuous rating can carry its emergency rating for exactly its emergency duration (Leitbild modelling choice).

sources.title: NERC PRC-023-4 Reliability Standard Audit Worksheet (transmission relay loadability)
sources.note: Load-responsive line relays must not operate at or below 150 % of the highest seasonal facility rating (PRC-023 R1 criterion 1, seen in NERC worksheet summaries, not in the standard text). The instantaneous element picks up at 150 % of the continuous rating, a simplified distance-zone load encroachment. The 1 s relay sample interval is a Leitbild modelling choice.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485 (SO GL), Annex III
sources.note: Table 1, Nordic: standard frequency range ±100 mHz, maximum steady-state frequency deviation 500 mHz, maximum instantaneous frequency deviation 1000 mHz. These set the priority 3, 2 and 1 island frequency bands; the 10 mHz (and 10 %) clear hysteresis is a Leitbild modelling choice.

sources.title: Commission Regulation (EU) 2017/1485 (SO GL), Article 25
sources.note: Branch loading alarms at the continuous rating (operational security limit) and at the emergency rating (transitory admissible overload) follow Article 25(1)(c); the 90 % pre-warning band is a Leitbild modelling choice.

sources.title: Leitbild alarm handling
sources.note: Leitbild modelling choices, not published values: an alarm changes state at most once per 10 s; clear delays of 10 s and raise delays of 0 s (10 s for the 90 % loading and reserve-deficit alarms); thresholds of 10 MW reserve deficit and 1 MW unserved load; priorities 1 for loss of supply, LFDD, AC non-convergence, branch trips, emergency loading and frequency beyond the instantaneous limit.
